newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: HK banks offer to fund Philippine power plant.
newsitem.headline: HK banks offer to fund Philippine power plant.

text.p: A group of Hong Kong financial firms, led by HSBC Investment Bank Asia, has offered to finance conversion of a mothballed Philippine nuclear plant into a 1,500-megawatt gas-fired power plant, an official of the Shell Group said on Thursday.

The official of Shell Philippines Exploration BV (Spex), a unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group, told reporters the offer was made to Shell by the representative of HSBC in Manila. The official asked not to be identified.
Shell recently signed a memorandum of understanding with state-owned National Power Corp (NPC) to study the possibility of converting the nuclear plant in nearby Bataan province to a gas-fired plant.
The consortium is composed of Hong Kong Shanghai Bank, Midland Bank, Hang Seng Bank, Marine Midland Bank, Samuel Montague and James Capel Securities.
The conversion has been estimated to cost $1 billion.
